title: Standard topology measures are likely insufficient to design or evolve memory

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Standard topology measures are likely insufficient to design or evolve memory

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because random networks matched to biological pathway models in number of nodes, edges, indegree, outdegree, betweenness, PageRank and hubness lack comparable memory, those structural features are not likely to be sufficient criteria for designing or evolving networks with memories.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Biswas S 2022, Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions › 3. Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Interestingly, since the random networks were designed to match the biological models in number of nodes, number of edges, indegree, outdegree, betweenness, PageRank, and hubness, those features are not likely to be sufficient criteria for designing (or evolving) networks with memories.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Biswas S, Clawson W, Levin M, “Learning in Transcriptional Network Models: Computational Discovery of Pathway-Level Memory and Effective Interventions”, International journal of molecular sciences (2022), doi:10.3390/ijms24010285; section “3. Discussion”. Scope: Gene regulatory and protein pathway networks

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-grn-learning-19: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The existing comparison can show that listed summaries do not uniquely determine memory in these models. The broader design-and-evolution conclusion extends beyond what this sample can decisively test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether networks matched on the listed measures still vary substantially in memory and whether adding those measures to predictive models yields useful out-of-sample performance. Failure of prediction supports insufficiency, but cannot exclude other uses in design.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nonsufficiency in this ensemble does not cover all design procedures.

Kinetic parameters and motifs remain unmatched confounders.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.58
data existence: 0.82
data adequacy: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The matching list and the memory comparison can be recomputed. A gap shows that this particular match is not sufficient inside this generator, which is weaker than the general design-and-evolution claim. Kinetics that were never matched remain a standing confound.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Generate random ODEs matched on node count, edge count, in- and out-degree, betweenness, PageRank and hubness, then compare their memory rates with the biological models. Similar memory despite the match would refute insufficiency of those features; a large memory gap would support insufficiency only for this generator.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Failure of one random generator does not show the features are useless for every design or evolutionary process.

Matching those summaries does not match kinetics, signs of regulation or motifs.
